extracted.intended_audience: readers of The Spectator / educated early-18th-century British public interested in manners, love, and domestic conduct
extracted.subtask_short: advice on manners, love, and domestic conduct
extracted.subtask_description: A series of Spectator essays giving practical and moral guidance on benevolence, courtship, marriage, needlework, and domestic virtue. The content mixes prescriptive rules, examples, and anecdotes to instruct readers in proper behaviour and choices in love and household life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation in worldly desires
rubrics_metrics.description: Desire not more of the World than is necessary to accommodate you in passing through it; look upon every thing beyond, not as useless only, but burthensome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place not your Quiet in Things, which you cannot have without putting others beside them, and thereby making them your Enemies; and which, when attain'd, will give you more Trouble to keep, than Satisfaction in the Enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of virtue as a communicable good
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue is a Good of a nobler kind; it grows by Communication, and so little resembles earthly Riches, that the more Hands it is lodged in, the greater is every Man's particular Stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By propagating and mingling their Fires, not only all the Lights of a Branch together cast a more extensive Brightness, but each single Light burns with a stronger Flame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wealth's greatest pleasure is doing good
rubrics_metrics.description: If Wealth be an Instrument of Pleasure, the greatest Pleasure it can put into your Power, is that of doing Good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider that the Organs of Sense act within a narrow Compass, and the Appetites will soon say they have enough; enlarging the sphere of happiness by sharing increases lasting pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contented mind enables benevolence
rubrics_metrics.description: A guilty, or a discontented Mind ... hath not Leisure to attend to the Necessity or Reasonableness of a Kindness desired, nor a Taste for those Pleasures which wait on Beneficence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The most miserable of all Beings is the most envious; as, on the other hand, the most communicative is the happiest. Place the Mind in its right Posture, it will immediately discover its innate Propension to Beneficence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose favourable timing for requests
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have a Favour to request of any one, to observe the softest times of Address, when the Soul, in a Flush of good Humour, takes a Pleasure to shew it self pleased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Persons conscious of their own integrity, satisfied with themselves, and their Condition, and full of Confidence in a Supreme Being, and the Hope of Immortality, survey all about them with a Flow of Good-will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate integrity and contentment to foster goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons conscious of their own integrity, satisfied with themselves ... survey all about them with a Flow of Good-will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such persons, like Trees which like their Soil, shoot out in Expressions of Kindness and bend beneath their own precious Load, to the hand of the Gatherer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attractiveness in courtship: reputation and notoriety
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no Person so irresistable as one who is a Man of Importance, provided it be in Matters of no Consequence. One who makes himself talked of ... is in a fair way of being a Favourite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a young Fellow made his Fortune by knocking down a Constable; notoriety (even for frivolous things) draws female curiosity and favour. 'His Reputation does more than half his Business.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Public behaviour and display increase favour
rubrics_metrics.description: In public spectacles (theatres, entries), being seen bowing to quality, seeming acquainted with the great, and making oneself important wins attention and affection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A man who can pretend acquaintances, bow to persons of rank, and appear versed in high company may make more advances in a day than months of courtship. Examples and Ovid translations illustrate tact for public shows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtship tactic: proximity and adaptive conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: At public shows sit close to the fair; find occasion to begin Discourse, enquire whose chariot this is, and suit all your inclinations to her mind; like what she likes, from thence your Court begin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be bold in taking the seat next to her; adapt to her tastes and the objects she favours to start and steer conversation in her favour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talk plausibly rather than obsess over strict truth
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk probably; no Matter for the Truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If need be, invent plausible names or facts, speak confidently of things unknown; probability and agreeable talk matter more in making an impression than absolute accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detecting affection in teasing and conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe whether you take a Secret Pride in making this Man of good Sense look very silly; whether you rejoice more when your behaviour makes your lover 'ready to hang himself'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such delight in provoking may signal a real underlying affection; emotional dynamics and mutual teasing can be signs of fondness rather than dislike.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marriage as joint interest and mutual care
rubrics_metrics.description: Married Persons must pursue one common Interest, and their united Care, for their Children; mutual Favours and Obligations naturally beget an Intense Affection in generous Minds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marriage produces both warmer love and more heartfelt hatred: mutual obligations increase both extremes; but the shared responsibilities encourage lasting attachment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow time for love to develop after marriage
rubrics_metrics.description: If she marries first, Love will come after. There are often many Faults conceal'd before Marriage, so there are sometimes many Virtues unobserv'd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Custom and constant conversation produce friendship and benevolence; imitation of speech and manners fosters affection over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation and habit produce mutual affection
rubrics_metrics.description: It is certain, that married Persons, who are possest with a mutual Esteem, not only catch the Air and way of Talk from one another, but fall into the same Traces of thinking and liking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imitation is a kind of artless Flattery and favors self-love; in time, partners may even resemble one another in features and manners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic arts as proper employment for women
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend the long neglected Art of Needle-work: Hours thrown away in Dress, Play, Visits ... were employ'd ... in writing out Receipts, or working Beds, Chairs, and Hangings for the Family.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Needlework is praised as a delightful entertainment, an outlet for genius, and a way to keep women out of harm's way and scandalous discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needlework prevents scandal and idle gossip
rubrics_metrics.description: This way of Life not only keeps fair Ladies from running out into Expences, but is at the same time an actual Improvement ... it takes them off from Scandal, the usual Attendant of Tea-Tables, and all other unactive Scenes of Life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While forming birds and beasts, neighbours will be allowed to be fathers of their own children; political disputes (Whig and Tory) will be less frequent where attention is on colours and stitches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needlework brings economic benefit to the family
rubrics_metrics.description: The Profit that is brought to the Family where these pretty Arts are encouraged ... not only keeps fair Ladies from running out into Expences, but is at the same time an actual Improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a matron could have inscribed that she 'Wrought out the whole Bible in Tapestry' and covered large domestic spaces, indicating durable domestic value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal: first addresses only in one's own embroidery
rubrics_metrics.description: That no young Virgin whatsoever be allow'd to receive the Addresses of her first Lover, but in a Suit of her own Embroidering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prescriptive rule intended to encourage industry, modesty, and productive restraint before courting; part of three proposed laws to restore needlework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal: display needlework before hiring servants
rubrics_metrics.description: That before every fresh Servant, she be oblig'd to appear with a new Stomacher at the least.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rule to ensure ongoing practice and visible industry as marks of household management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal: marriage only after household work is prepared
rubrics_metrics.description: That no one be actually married, till she hath the Child-bed Pillows, &c. ready Stitched, as likewise the Mantle for the Boy quite finished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical requirement to ensure readiness for domestic duties and to encourage thrift and preparedness before entering marriage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use productive work to occupy time and resist temptation
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ the Hours in imitating Fruits and Flowers, transplanting all the Beauties of Nature into their own Dress, or raising a new Creation in their Closets and Apartments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even those without genius should work, if only to keep them out of Harm's way; working fills idle hours that otherwise encourage vice or scandal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discretion as a necessary qualification in a husband
rubrics_metrics.description: Discretion seems absolutely necessary, and accordingly we find that the best Husbands have been most famous for their Wisdom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Homeric and classical references (Ulysses, Brutus) show that prudence and wisdom are foundational for domestic fidelity and good household government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtue produces constancy and mutual esteem
rubrics_metrics.description: Virtue is the next necessary Qualification for this domestick Character, as it naturally produces Constancy and mutual Esteem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing Brutus and Porcia as examples: moral character fosters reliable affection and respect in marriage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good-nature and even temper in marriage
rubrics_metrics.description: Good-Nature is a third necessary Ingredient ... Good-Nature is insufficient, unless it be steady and uniform, and accompanied with an Evenness of Temper, which is, above all things, to be preserved in this Friendship contracted for Life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evenness of temper, steadiness, and uniform good-nature attract admiration and are essential to sustain long-term domestic friendship; philosophical exemplars like Socrates and Marcus Aurelius illustrate composed minds making good husbands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise forbearance in the first year
rubrics_metrics.description: If the wedded Pair would but habituate themselves for the first Year to bear with one another's Faults, the Difficulty would be pretty well conquer'd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit counsel to practice patience early in marriage as a practical method to overcome initial frictions and establish mutual harmony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive curiosity about the future
rubrics_metrics.description: The Desire of knowing future Events is one of the strongest Inclinations in the Mind of Man ... If we consider that we are free Agents, we shall discover the Absurdity of Enquiries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skeptical advice against superstition and divination; accept ignorance regarding future events, rely on reason and accept the enhancement of unexpected pleasures.
